overall_summary: Extreme space facts and exoplanet 'What If' scenarios focusing on hostile environments, extreme weather, and cosmic dangers consistently drive the highest views and engagement. Conversely, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts struggle to gain traction, often failing to surpass double-digit views.

winning_patterns.pattern: What If You Fell Into... / Extreme Exoplanet Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (838 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,025 views), and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' (490 views) are the channel's top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on the 'What If You Fell Into [Extreme Planet]' format, using highly visual, hostile planetary environments as the core subject.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Molten Iron!' (349 views) performed significantly better than generic weather titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanet weather around high-value or highly dangerous materials (e.g., glass, rubies, iron) to trigger instant curiosity.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads), 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views), and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently underperformed.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from cognitive psychology and brain hacks, or reframe them through a high-stakes survival or mystery lens.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' (10 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Rock!' (49 views) failed to capture interest compared to active, high-stakes framing.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive titles; instead, use active, high-stakes framing like 'What If You Visited...' or 'This Planet Will Break Your Brain!'.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet in the Universe?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a completely black screen and a sudden, deep heartbeat sound effect, asking: 'What if you fell into a planet darker than coal?'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being pitch black and absorbing 99% of light, the planet is actually a boiling-hot hellscape of 1,800°F, glowing with a silent, demonic red light.
next_video.reason: TrES-2b is already a proven high-performer on the channel. Combining this high-interest subject with the highly engaging 'What If You Fell Into...' format and a 21-second duration maximizes the probability of high retention and viral reach.

experiment: Test the 'What If You Fell Into...' format on a deep-ocean mystery (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into the Massive Waterfall Hidden Under the Ocean?') to see if the high-performing space hook style translates successfully to geography and oceanography.
